      <title>How African philosophies inspired a new approach to staging film festivals in Manchester</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/08/african-philosophies-see-my-world-film-festival-manchester</link>
      <description><p>See My World, an event highlighting the pan-African thought via film, poetry and dance, builds on momentum sparked by local activists and creatives</p><p>African philosophies including exploring how lessons from the past can shape the present and near future have inspired a film festival coming to Manchester.</p><p><a href="https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/e/see-my-world-film-festival-tickets-2000609164867">See My World</a>, a day dedicated to independent creators from across the African diaspora in the north of England, will take place at the Contact theatre on 21 November.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/08/african-philosophies-see-my-world-film-festival-manchester">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years for murder of 190 children</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie</link>
      <description><p>Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families</p><p>The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history.</p><p>The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/kenya-starvation-cult-leader-guilty-murder-190-children">found the cult leader guilty</a> of the crimes.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>ANC faces bruising defeat in South African local elections with 80% of ballots counted</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/anc-faces-defeat-south-african-local-elections</link>
      <description><p>Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result</p><p>The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80% of ballots counted.</p><p>Wednesday’s fragmented vote marks another stage in the decline of the ANC, which has led national governments since the end of white minority apartheid rule in 1994. High unemployment, crime, corruption and poor local service delivery have all contributed to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/04/anc-south-africa-local-elections-water-outages-power-cuts">voters turning away from the party</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/anc-faces-defeat-south-african-local-elections">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/04/british-healthcare-worker-ebola-evacuated-drc-to-uk-document-shows</link>
      <description><p>Patient is ⁠in ​stable condition and will be transferred to a specialist ‘high consequence’ infectious disease unit</p><p>A British healthcare worker with Ebola is being evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the UK for medical treatment, it has been confirmed.</p><p>“A British citizen currently in the DR Congo has tested positive for Ebola,” a spokesperson for the UK government said in a statement on Wednesday. “The UK has well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this, and those processes have been activated … The risk to the UK public from Ebola remains low.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/04/british-healthcare-worker-ebola-evacuated-drc-to-uk-document-shows">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>ANC faces anger over poor services as South Africans vote in local elections</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/04/anc-south-africa-local-elections-water-outages-power-cuts</link>
      <description><p>Party expected to get less than a third of the vote amid frustration over water outages and power cuts</p><p>The African National Congress is on course for a bruising result in South Africa’s local elections on Wednesday as voters go to the polls amid deep discontent over water outages, power cuts and crumbling infrastructure.</p><p>The former liberation movement, which Nelson Mandela led to power in 1994 at the end of apartheid as South Africa’s first black president, is still likely to be the largest party. However, polls showed it getting less than a third of the vote, down from 45.6% at the <a href="https://results.elections.org.za/dashboards/lge/">last municipal elections</a> in 2021 and 40.2% in <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/article/2024/jun/02/south-africa-election-anc-coalition-talks-ramaphosa">2024’s national elections</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/04/anc-south-africa-local-elections-water-outages-power-cuts">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Pope’s visit to Argentina sets up showdown with ‘hyper-capitalist’ Milei</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/08/popes-visit-to-argentina-sets-up-showdown-with-hyper-capitalist-milei</link>
      <description><p>President has opposing views on many issues, and once called Leo’s predecessor the ‘representative of the Evil One’</p><p>Trees are being planted in the garden. The brightly coloured buildings are getting another coat of paint. The choir rehearses. Hundreds of other residents, several of them using wheelchairs, practise their positions outside the sanctuary. Excitement is in the air, because on Monday 9 November, the Cottolengo Don Orione – a Catholic-run home for disabled people – will be the first stop on Pope Leo XIV’s first full day of his trip to Argentina.</p><p>But the pope’s visit to Claypole, about 26km from Buenos Aires, does not come at an especially happy time for the home, which counts about 400 residents with disabilities. Argentina’s president, Javier Milei, has made wide-ranging cuts to disability funding.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/08/popes-visit-to-argentina-sets-up-showdown-with-hyper-capitalist-milei">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Farmers face big drop in production from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event</p><p>Banana producers in Latin America are calling for better pay to help cope with the impact of the climate crisis, as they face big drops in production resulting from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event.</p><p>High winds in parts of Colombia, one of the biggest suppliers to the UK market where droughts are predicted in some regions this year, and heavy rainfall in Peru and Ecuador are already affecting production, according to the Fairtrade Foundation ethical trade body.       <description><p>High-stakes talks involving 190 countries begin on Monday as world grapples with El Niño supercharged by fossil fuels</p><p>The <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/08/cop31-what-is-at-stake-at-the-un-climate-summit-and-what-can-it-achieve">Cop31 summit</a> must produce progress, “a tangible outcome ... that people can see is real”, its host has said as <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/08/cop31-key-players-climate-talks">scores of world leaders and representatives of close to 190 countries</a> gather in Turkey for the UN climate talks.</p><p>The high-stakes meeting begins on Monday, as countries around the world grapple with the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/sep/21/super-el-nino-temperature-record">strongest El Niño weather system on record</a>, supercharged by fossil fuels, which is set to take hundreds of thousands of lives and cause damage costing trillions of dollars.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/08/cop31-climate-summit-deliver-progress-real-host-says">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Who’s who at Cop31: key players at the climate talks</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/08/cop31-key-players-climate-talks</link>
      <description><p>What are the relationships and dominant interests in play, as the summit kicks off after a bitter row over its hosting?</p><p>Hosting Cop was a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/audio/2021/oct/25/australia-v-the-climate-part-1-kyoto">key pledge from Australia’s prime minister, Anthony Albanese in 2021</a>, while in opposition, before his successful election campaign. But arcane rules meant <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/commentisfree/2022/sep/19/australia-is-pushing-to-host-a-cop-meeting-if-successful-it-would-be-forced-to-ramp-up-climate-action">the country had to wait its turn to bid</a> and was then <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2025/jun/28/albanese-will-need-to-resolve-the-standoff-with-turkey-if-australia-is-to-host-cop31">embroiled in an angry row with Turkey over the hosting</a>. The final compromise put Australia in charge of the negotiations which will take place in the Turkish city of Antalya. The bitter taste left by the row lingers and Australia has seemed to some a rather half-hearted host. The country’s media has been much quieter on Cop than previous host countries, and although Albanese will speak at the opening of the leaders’ segment, he is unlikely to stay long.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/08/cop31-key-players-climate-talks">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/08/uk-zombie-brexit-border-inspection-posts-check-goods</link>
      <description><p>Five of seven facilities in England and Wales never reached operational stage as Tories vacillated over plans to check goods</p><p>The UK wasted at least £100m in taxpayers’ money to set up zombie Brexit border inspection posts that were never used, it has been revealed.</p><p>The overall cost of Brexit was put at an <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/article/2024/may/20/britain-brexit-border-checks-eu-cost-uk-firms-470m-a-year-says-watchdog">estimated £4.7bn</a> by the National Audit Office last year but this included years-long transformation of the software used for customs declarations and other systems built to cope with the UK leaving the single market.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/08/uk-zombie-brexit-border-inspection-posts-check-goods">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Polish prosecutors open terrorism investigation into Kraków shooting</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/08/krakow-shooting-poland-terrorism-investigation</link>
      <description><p>Six people killed in attack probably inspired by far right, according to officials, as police say suspect’s parents and sister found dead at his home</p><p>Polish prosecutors have opened a terrorism investigation after a 24-year-old man <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/07/krakow-poland-shooting-market-square-deaths-gunman">opened fire in a busy market square</a> in Kraków, killing six people including a Briton and injuring 17, in an attack that authorities said was probably inspired by far-right ideologies.</p><p>Police confirmed on Sunday that three people found dead at the gunman’s home after the attack on Saturday afternoon were his father, 53, mother, 52, and sister, 21.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/08/krakow-shooting-poland-terrorism-investigation">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Luc Corlouër made ‘deal’ with Prix Goncourt winner Philippe Jaenada over his research into model Louise Cansot, murdered in Paris in 1949</p><p>For almost eight decades the artists’ model Louise Cansot, the subject of the novel winning France’s most prestigious literary prize this year, was one of Paris’s forgotten murder victims.</p><p>After her body was found near the Seine in September 1949, city police wrote off the young woman, immortalised as “the girl of 100 portraits”, as loose, libertine and – worse – an unmarried mother.       <title>Briton among six dead after gunman opens fire in Kraków market square</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/07/krakow-poland-shooting-market-square-deaths-gunman</link>
      <description><p>Three more people found dead at home of suspect, who minister says held ‘ultra-nationalistic’ views</p><p>Six people were killed and 16 wounded after a gunman opened fire in a busy market square in Kraków, authorities said, in what Poland’s defence minister called an “act of terror” on the people of the city.</p><p>The suspect, a 25-year-old Polish citizen, opened fire with an automatic weapon in the city’s main square at about 3pm on Saturday before being apprehended by police.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/07/krakow-poland-shooting-market-square-deaths-gunman">Continue reading...</a></description>

An insider look at French politics, culture, society, technology and sport through on-the-ground reports, investigations, exclusive interviews, debates and analyses.</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Sun, 08 Nov 2026 14:20:12 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>French students vow to continue protests despite concessions from Macron govt</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261026-macron-vows-concrete-measures-to-address-student-demands-after-unrest</link><description>
French student leaders on Monday called for more protests despite President Emmanuel Macron's pledge of  "concrete and strong" measures to address their demands after weeks of nationwide unrest. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu met with high school representatives alongside education ministers to announce follow-up action ranging from a total overhaul of higher education admissions platform Parcoursup to a cap on class sizes.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ade564d2-d134-11f1-9bc8-6d20ccb9a352</guid><pubDate>Mon, 26 Oct 2026 12:25:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg">© Aurelien Morissard, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Controversial West African activist Kemi Seba detained in Paris</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20241015-controversial-west-african-activist-kemi-seba-detained-in-paris</link><description>
Kemi Seba, a controversial African activist known for his virulent anti-Western stance, has been arrested in Paris, a source close to the case told AFP Tuesday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d792557e-8afa-11ef-b7b5-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_1U53IC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d792557e-8afa-11ef-b7b5-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_1U53IC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b9cb5c02-8aff-11ef-811f-005056a97652</guid><pubDate>Tue, 15 Oct 2024 14:17:13 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d792557e-8afa-11ef-b7b5-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_1U53IC.jpg">© Stéphane de Sakutin, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France’s new health pass rules raise questions as many scramble to adapt</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20210714-france-s-new-health-pass-rules-raise-questions-as-many-scramble-to-adapt</link><description>
While the extension of France’s health pass and other new anti-Covid 19 measures announced by President Emmanuel Macron Monday night are yet to be hammered out in detail, what’s certain is that a full-throttled return to a normal life of frequenting café terraces, restaurants, cinemas, theatres and other culture and leisure activities will now hinge on having a pass sanitaire (or health pass).
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/95a7a1f4-e018-11eb-931e-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/61be21e7dd8409eb6f2604b7d2e8d59f8e2865dc.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/95a7a1f4-e018-11eb-931e-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/61be21e7dd8409eb6f2604b7d2e8d59f8e2865dc.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5823e86e-e4b0-11eb-8c07-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 16:03:14 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/95a7a1f4-e018-11eb-931e-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/61be21e7dd8409eb6f2604b7d2e8d59f8e2865dc.jpg">© Sameer Al-Doumy, AFP</source><dc:creator>Romain BRUNET</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Daughter loses legal case in bitter Asterix family feud</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/20131211-daughter-loses-legal-case-bitter-asterix-family-feud-france-comics</link><description>A long-running family feud between Asterix co-creator Albert Uderzo and his daughter took a new twist on Tuesday after judges dismissed a claim by Sylvie Uderzo that her father was mentally frail and being exploited.</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/abe23e78-093f-11e9-b87e-005056a964fe/w:1024/p:16x9/asterix_0.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/abe23e78-093f-11e9-b87e-005056a964fe/w:1024/p:16x9/asterix_0.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">563894c2-cafc-11e7-8241-005056bf73c0</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Dec 2013 18:09:33 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/abe23e78-093f-11e9-b87e-005056a964fe/w:1024/p:16x9/asterix_0.jpg">Photo: AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macron says 'racist terrorist attack’ in Trappes marks turning point for France</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261023-french-prosecutors-investigate-paris-shooting-as-suspected-terror-attack</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron described Friday’s drive-by shooting in the western suburb of Trappes as a “terrorist and racist attack”, saying it marks a turning point for France. One person was killed and at least four people, including a 12-year-old girl, were wounded in the shooting, apparently at random. Two of the victims have immigrant backgrounds.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">72670cfa-ced0-11f1-8bc7-bb90dbb6a8a1</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 11:08:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg">© Hannah McKay, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Top contemporary French artist Christian Boltanski dies aged 76</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20210714-top-contemporary-french-artist-christian-boltanski-dies-aged-76</link><description>
Christian Boltanski, one of France's top contemporary artists whose multimedia works probed the meaning of mortality and memory, has died aged 76, a former museum director told AFP on Sunday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b7135ce8-e4c8-11eb-89be-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 18:44:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg">© Miguel Riopa, AFP</source><dc:creator>NEWS WIRES</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macron says world leaders have made 'stupid' comments on France riots based on fake AI videos</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261021-macron-says-world-leaders-have-made-stupid-comments-on-france-riots-based-on-fake-ai-videos</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron took aim at world leaders including US President Donald Trump for trying to exploit the riots and looting that broke out alongside peaceful demonstrations in France Saturday for their own political advantage. Another wave of demonstrations against France's worsening cost of living is planned for the coming Saturday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2c665312-cd42-11f1-8dbc-290623bfb92e</guid><pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:48:11 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg">© Benoit Tessier, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Teen wounds headmaster and teacher after opening fire at French school</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261012-french-police-arrest-14-year-old-after-two-teaching-staff-wounded-by-hunting-rifle-fire</link><description>
Two teaching staff were shot and wounded by a 14-year-old boy armed with a hunting rifle at a school in Aubagne near Marseille Monday morning, French Education Minister ‌Édouard Geffray said. Authorities said the teenager's father had been taken into custody and that there did not seem to be any link to the student protests that have swept across the country in recent weeks. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">de062bda-c61f-11f1-828c-2d5a86616301</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:43:38 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg">© Lou Benoist, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Focus</category><title>How the French army trains for 'high-intensity' combat</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/focus/20210714-how-the-french-army-trains-for-high-intensity-conflict</link><description>
France's new military programming law increases the country's defence budget to 2 percent of GDP by 2025. It's an investment in the modernisation of equipment, but also in the training of soldiers. The aim is to teach soldiers to face an army at least as well equipped as that of France in a context of global rearmament. Our reporters Fadile Bhayat, Mandi Heshmati and Caroline Grandjean followed French troops during a "high-intensity" training exercise.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">023ce07e-e41d-11eb-a94a-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 14:42:34 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Fadile BHAYAT</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight</category><title>Raphaël Glucksmann, the man who wants to be French president</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/spotlight/20261011-a-profile-of-rapha%C3%ABl-glucksmann-the-man-who-wants-to-be-french-president</link><description>
Raphaël Glucksmann has won the primary to represent the French centre-left in the upcoming presidential elections, securing 66% of the vote. He now faces the challenge of building support for the centre-left in a political landscape where the far right, led by Marine Le Pen, remains a major force.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b6534792-c59a-11f1-b235-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/Raphael-Glucksmann-000-D2X49DY.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b6534792-c59a-11f1-b235-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/Raphael-Glucksmann-000-D2X49DY.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">99b61d02-c596-11f1-9bf5-777190d2ada5</guid><pubDate>Sun, 11 Oct 2026 17:50:02 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Gavin LEE</dc:creator></item><item><category>Perspective</category><title>'A lot of French politicians are out of touch with a large part of the population'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/perspective/20220209-a-lot-of-french-politicians-are-out-of-touch-with-a-large-part-of-the-population</link><description>
Our guest is Fabien Truong, a sociologist, author and associate professor at the University of Paris. A former schoolteacher, he spent a decade following the lives of around 20 of his students, charting their progress from the time they took their end of school exams to when they finished their higher education. Those 10 years took in the riots that rocked France back in 2005 to the terror attacks of January 2015. He gives us his take on the French presidential election campaign, as seen from the suburbs.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a29e27fe-89a3-11ec-8742-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-13035161446203b32c2451f2.07563475.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a29e27fe-89a3-11ec-8742-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-13035161446203b32c2451f2.07563475.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2534ffb8-8980-11ec-8ce4-005056a97652</guid><pubDate>Wed, 09 Feb 2022 12:31:33 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Sharon GAFFNEY</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Fire destroys Paris's oldest covered food market</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261012-fire-burns-down-paris-s-oldest-covered-food-market</link><description>
A fire "completely destroyed" Paris's historic Marché Couvert des Enfants Rouges early Monday, authorities said. The cause of the fire that swept through the capital's oldest covered food market remains unknown. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c5504c60-c610-11f1-b48e-936bba59cf88</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:02:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg">© Creative Commons</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'Tefal campaign': with Covid-19 monopolising voters' minds, nothing sticks</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20220209-tefal-campaign-pandemic-prudent-president-keep-french-election-race-on-the-backburner</link><description>
Presidential campaigns offer an abundance of catch phrases, whether slogans finessed by a candidate's team to deliver maximum impact or coined spontaneously on the trail. The proclamations – and gaffes – of presidential hopefuls bring texture to an election race and come to define a campaign, whether for a news cycle or forever in the history books. FRANCE 24 brings you the buzzwords of the 2022 French presidential race. In the spotlight: "Tefal campaign".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f4e47fa4-88f4-11ec-97bf-005056a97652</guid><pubDate>Wed, 09 Feb 2022 10:43:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png">© FMM Graphic Studio</source><dc:creator>Tracy MCNICOLL</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French police clash with teens blockading schools as unions stage day of protests</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-french-police-clash-with-teens-blockading-schools-as-union-stage-day-of-protests</link><description>
French teenagers on Tuesday clashed with police as they kept up a blockade of high schools in cities across the country to demand better conditions and more teacher hirings. The escalating standoff came as unions staged a day of demonstrations against a cost-cutting budget drafted by Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu's embattled government.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b23ed102-bbeb-11f1-861d-cf265369200f</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:53:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg">© Sameer Al-Doumy, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Legion of Honour: Police investigate corruption claims for France’s top award</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-legion-of-honour-police-investigate-corruption-claims-for-france-s-top-award</link><description>
French police took a top general into custody last week as part of an ongoing probe into potential bribery among the selection committee for the country’s highest decoration, the Legion of Honour. Investigations centre on possible payoffs for awards including expensive meals, holidays and thousands of euros in cash.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cf7e5750-bc0f-11f1-9d67-9d40f7c16032</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:43:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg">© Francois Mori, AP</source><dc:creator>Joanna YORK</dc:creator></item><item><category>France 2022: The Choice</category><title>Battle for the French far right: Zemmour, Le Pen try to steal each other's thunder</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/france-2022-the-campaign/20220207-battle-for-the-far-right-zemmour-le-pen-fight-to-steal-each-other-s-thunder</link><description>
As France's April presidential election approaches, the campaign is getting under way in earnest. In this edition of our new show, we focus on the French Communist Party attempting a political comeback and discuss at length the battle raging between Eric Zemmour and Marine Le Pen for leadership of the French far right. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b99fd93a-885d-11ec-9917-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/XX%20NW%20OOV%20SPLIT%20LE%20PEN%20ZEMMOUR.transfer001.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b99fd93a-885d-11ec-9917-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/XX%20NW%20OOV%20SPLIT%20LE%20PEN%20ZEMMOUR.transfer001.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6ecf0724-8861-11ec-862b-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Mon, 07 Feb 2022 22:00:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Marc PERELMAN</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Eiffel Tower chief to step down over removal of women staff during Hindu group's visit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-eiffel-tower-chief-to-step-down-over-removal-of-women-staff-during-hindu-group-visit-baps</link><description>
The head of the Eiffel Tower is set to step down in the wake of a controversy sparked by the removal of female workers during a private visit of the Paris landmark by members of the Hindu sect BAPS, which triggered a staff walkout earlier this month and sparked outrage in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b85f821e-bc10-11f1-89fe-7b0f1abdd3bc</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:22:29 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France's Le Pen vows to 'counterattack' after top ally Bardella hit by anti-Semitism claims</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-france-s-le-pen-vows-to-counterattack-after-top-ally-bardella-hit-by-anti-semitism-claims</link><description>
French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen on Tuesday denounced an attempt to "derail" her Élysée Palace run after a media report accused the head of her far-right National Rally (RN) party, Jordan Bardella, of making ant-Semitic comments in 2013. Le Pen said Bardella, who is tipped to be prime minister if she wins the presidency, had her "total confidence".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0b97a704-bc02-11f1-8bbb-ad34ceb9e2f1</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 12:33:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France puts out massive fire that torched 42,000 hectares and smouldered for 69 days</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260928-france-puts-out-massive-fire-that-torched-42-000-hectares-and-smouldered-for-69-days</link><description>
France's largest wildfire since 1949 has been declared extinguished more than two months after it broke out in southwestern Gironde, forcing the evacuation of around 224,000 people and covering the city of Bordeaux with a thick plume of smoke. The blaze was put under control on August 1, but continued to smoulder underground for weeks.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f68114c-bb5e-11f1-a5f5-19c8c18b5c0d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 28 Sep 2026 17:00:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg">© Julien De Rosa, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-far-right-politician-%C3%A9ric-zemmour-joins-2027-french-presidential-race</link><description>
French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2e6bcd08-b33a-11f1-b960-e76b244d1c83</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:06:31 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg">© Emma Da Silva, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-french-pm-vows-to-cut-public-spending-by-%E2%82%AC54-billion-to-reduce-deficit</link><description>
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61b975d6-b32e-11f1-ab9e-b5bbc83805db</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 07:23:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Radio France staff strike over appointment of far-right weekly editor</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260913-radio-france-staff-strike-over-appointment-of-far-right-weekly-editor</link><description>
Staff at public broadcaster Radio France began a two-day strike on Sunday over the appointment of Charles Sapin, deputy editor-in-chief at far-right weekly Valeurs Actuelles. Unions accuse Sapin of promoting far-right ideas ahead of next spring's presidential election, while management has defended the appointment in the name of pluralism.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/02d53bbe-af04-11f1-9d7b-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/e1d9fdbe2d48d1241c3b6d21d639c8533611857e.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/02d53bbe-af04-11f1-9d7b-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/e1d9fdbe2d48d1241c3b6d21d639c8533611857e.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5ef9108e-af70-11f1-8f8f-7db7cf189a1f</guid><pubDate>Sun, 13 Sep 2026 12:44:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/02d53bbe-af04-11f1-9d7b-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/e1d9fdbe2d48d1241c3b6d21d639c8533611857e.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France apologises for diplomatic spat with US to lift block on new ambassador to Washington</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260913-france-apologises-for-diplomatic-spat-with-us-to-lift-block-on-new-ambassador-to-washington</link><description>
The French UN mission said it regretted an online post criticising a US vote at the UN General Assembly in a move that should clear the way for the new French ambassador Aurélien Lechevallier to take up his post in Washington.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8728c102-af4e-11f1-9048-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C2P7793.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8728c102-af4e-11f1-9048-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C2P7793.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">9c8e07e2-af4d-11f1-8c62-892c781611bd</guid><pubDate>Sun, 13 Sep 2026 09:01:17 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8728c102-af4e-11f1-9048-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C2P7793.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French wine yields drop to new historic low after searing summer heat</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260907-scorching-summer-pushes-french-wine-harvest-to-new-historic-low</link><description>
French wine production is expected to suffer its worst harvest in some 70 years with the agriculture ministry on Monday forecasting a 6 percent drop in output after a summer of scorching temperatures, heatwaves and drought. France last week announced more than €1 billion in emergency support for farmers.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/45a0454c-aab3-11f1-8ad4-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/f0e62229cbdd19e6bec50a391c5d77395a3a4af6.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/45a0454c-aab3-11f1-8ad4-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/f0e62229cbdd19e6bec50a391c5d77395a3a4af6.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4694cc16-aab3-11f1-81c9-ff9d54eec782</guid><pubDate>Mon, 07 Sep 2026 11:57:17 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/45a0454c-aab3-11f1-8ad4-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/f0e62229cbdd19e6bec50a391c5d77395a3a4af6.jpg">© Sebastien Salom-Gomis, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France targets Shein and Temu with new fast fashion levy</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260831-france-targets-shein-and-temu-with-new-fast-fashion-levy</link><description><![CDATA[
Starting this week, France will charge a penalty on cheaply made clothing sold by ultra-fast fashion retailers, with the fee reaching nearly €20 per item by 2030. Aimed at platforms like Shein, Temu and AliExpress, the levy follows a June law targeting disposable fashion's environmental toll, though rival brands like H&M and Zara are exempt.
]]></description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b81f0872-a55b-11f1-bfba-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-08-31T095850Z-1200926585-RC27HIARHQ0D-RTRMADP-3-SHEIN-IPO.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b81f0872-a55b-11f1-bfba-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-08-31T095850Z-1200926585-RC27HIARHQ0D-RTRMADP-3-SHEIN-IPO.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5a3534ae-a554-11f1-b888-bf56321c7dab</guid><pubDate>Mon, 31 Aug 2026 15:55:12 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b81f0872-a55b-11f1-bfba-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-08-31T095850Z-1200926585-RC27HIARHQ0D-RTRMADP-3-SHEIN-IPO.jpg">© Jorge Silva, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <title>Trump may have lost but don’t bet Democrats can fix the economy</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/07/democrats-economy-affordability-crisis</link>
      <description><p>There’s not much they can do over the next couple of years to alleviate angry voters’ stress over prices</p><p>It was the economy, again. Although Donald Trump largely ignored it, voters’ acute concerns over the rising cost of living fuelled a political upheaval for the ages that is likely to deliver the biggest swing toward Democrats since Watergate, granting them the largest House majority in nearly four decades alongside their biggest edge in the Senate since 2008.</p><p>Still, having come to power promising to restore affordability, the new crop of Democrats are soon to discover that there is not much they can do over the next couple of years to alleviate angry voters’ stress over pricey gas and groceries, exorbitant mortgages and unaffordable healthcare.</p><p>Eduardo Porter is a journalist focused on economics and politics. He writes the newsletter <a href="https://eduardoelreportero.substack.com/">Being There</a> on Substack</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/07/democrats-economy-affordability-crisis">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>‘Low-hire, low-fire’ labor market shows sluggish growth but few layoffs, with an interest rate hike expected in December</p><p>The US added 165,000 jobs to the economy in October, a sign of resilience in the labor market amid ongoing war in the Middle East and inflation, according to new data released on Friday.</p><p>Economists had said the labor market has been stuck in a “low-hire, low-fire” state, in which job growth is sluggish but layoffs also remain low, but October’s data surpassed economist expectations. The <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/usemployment">unemployment rate</a> went down slightly to 4.1%, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/06/us-job-growth-october">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Rural voters were feeling left behind before the midterms, poll shows</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/05/former-trump-voters-economy</link>
      <description><p>Polling done for the Guardian shows plummeting support from a former key constituency of Donald Trump’s base</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/community/live/2026/nov/05/what-happens-after-the-blue-wave-our-reporters-answer-your-midterm-election-results-questions">Q&amp;A: Ask your questions about Democrats’ win in the midterms</a></p></li></ul><p>Polling conducted by the Harris Poll for the Guardian before the election shows just how angry voters were and points to one key reason Republicans lost so badly: plummeting support from rural voters, once a key constituency of Donald Trump’s base.</p><p>Over the summer, 95% of Americans indicated they believed there was an <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/jul/07/cost-of-living-poll-groceries-gas">affordability crisis</a>, particularly because of steep gas and grocery prices. By October, 61% of voters <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/15/voters-economy-cost-of-living-prices-poll">believed</a> the country was experiencing a recession, even though technically it wasn’t.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/05/former-trump-voters-economy">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>US stocks rise, dollar slides as investors digest Democrats’ midterm victories</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/04/us-dollar-slides-democrats-midterm-election-win-growth-fears</link>
      <description><p>Government bond yields fall while initial fears ease over impact of election results on world’s biggest economy</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/nov/04/midterm-elections-results-senate-house-michigan-maine-mississippi-latest-updates">US midterm elections – live updates</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/04/explainer-midterms-trump-us-global-economy-markets">After US midterms, what will lame-duck Trump mean for global economy?</a></p></li></ul><p>US stocks have surged as investors digest the Democrats’ victories in the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/us-midterm-elections-2026">midterm elections</a>, lifted by hopes that <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/donaldtrump">Donald Trump</a>’s turbulent policymaking would be restrained and shaking off initial fears about the impact on growth in the world’s largest economy.</p><p>The Dow Jones rose close to 3%, its best day in over a year, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq and the benchmark S&amp;P 500 gained about 1.5% each when markets closed on Wednesday afternoon, turning around overnight falls in US stock futures after the news that the Democratic party <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/nov/03/midterm-election-results-live-updates">won control</a> of the Senate and the House of Representatives.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/04/us-dollar-slides-democrats-midterm-election-win-growth-fears">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>CVS Pharmacy will be separate from CVS Health, housing major insurer Aetna and benefits manager Caremark</p><p>CVS Health, the largest US healthcare conglomerate valued at $117bn, has announced its plans split off its pharmacy chain from its <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/money/healthinsurance">health insurance</a> and benefits businesses, ending an era in which healthcare companies grew into vast conglomerates.</p><p>In their announcement on Wednesday, CVS Health said they will split off its 9,000 pharmacies, in-store clinics and mail order prescription business into a business named CVS Pharmacy.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/04/cvs-health-pharmacy-insurance">Continue reading...</a></description>

Already unfathomably wealthy, Silicon Valley tycoons believed a Maga-sized public shift to the right would enrich them even more. It did. For several years, while Trump seemed an everlasting kingmaker and AI’s expansion seemed unstoppable, their fortunes ballooned to values beyond comprehension. Elon Musk’s surpassed $1tn.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/05/tech-barons-america-musk-bezos-zuckerberg">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>The survival of American democracy depends on taxing billionaires</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/27/democracy-tax-billionaires</link>
      <description><p>It is essential not just to fund the public goods the nation needs, it is indispensable to restore a sense of fairness</p><p>Money doesn’t buy happiness, we’re told. Even some economists agree. The Nobel prize-winning economists Daniel Kahneman and Angus Deaton once <a href="https://www.pnas.org/doi/full/10.1073/pnas.1011492107">proposed that</a> rising income increased people’s emotional wellbeing only up to a ceiling of about $115,000 in today’s money.</p><p>They probably hadn’t met many billionaires. The ultra-rich may not pursue happiness in the joyful sense of the word. But they will try every trick in the book to hang on to their stash and woe betide the tax authority that tries to lay a finger on their treasure.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/27/democracy-tax-billionaires">Continue reading...</a></description>
